about: The interaction contract as data (Prompt 155; INTERACTION.md is the prose). tests/interactionContract.test.js holds every registered surface to it. Prompt 278 activated the pending checks, registered every drag it found and added the walk inventory: one row for every surface of the navigation inventory, walked by e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js in both languages.

actions.nudge: Move a quantity or an aim by one step; Alt is a quarter of a step, Shift is four.
actions.along: Previous and next along an ordered set (Left, Right).
actions.across: Previous and next across the set's series (Up, Down).
actions.page: A surface-declared jump along the set (PageUp, PageDown).
actions.confirm: Commit what is aimed or toggle the focused item (Enter; Space where the item is a toggle).
actions.cancel: Abandon, clear or close the innermost thing (Escape).
actions.zoom: Zoom a camera in or out where a surface has one (+ or =, -).

noBareKey.openTable: The surface's Table control, reached with Tab. T is the theme everywhere.
noBareKey.openDisclosure: Enter or Space on the disclosure's summary, which the browser provides.

meanings: extend the selection (plot, image and table selection)
conflicts.resolution: Shift is the coarse size on a surface that nudges a number. A selection surface keeps Shift to extend and uses PageUp and PageDown for its coarse step. The 3-D camera keeps Shift to pan; a proposed rename (pan on Ctrl) is a decision for Carl, because it changes a binding students and instructors may have been taught.

meanings: pans the view left (A, W, S, D beside the arrows)
conflicts.resolution: One press of A did both. Measured on 2026-10-19 with a type armed: the view moved 40 px and a keyboard placement began. Resolved by Prompt 278: with a type armed A arms the placement and no longer pans (js/placement.js); with nothing armed A pans as W, S and D do, and the arrow keys always pan. e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js, 'A arms a placement and does not also pan'.

The two never share a page. The contract assigns + and - to zoom; the sandbox keeps them for speed, and since Prompt 278 its zoom is the view pad's two buttons, reached with Tab and pressed with Enter or one pointer (interaction.keyboard.sandbox-zoom). Moving speed to another pair, so that + and - could zoom in the sandbox too, is still a decision for Carl.

drags.gesture: Press where the body goes and drag to throw it; the length of the drag is its speed.
alternatives: Precise placement: a form that takes the position, velocity and mass as numbers and calls the same placeBody().
Keyboard aim: A arms it, the arrows aim, Enter commits, with the drag's own velocity expression.

drags.gesture: Drag empty space to move the view.
alternatives: The view pad in Tools: four buttons move the view a step, two zoom it about its center.
The arrow keys and W, A, S, D pan; Home resets.

drags.gesture: Drag across a plot to select the rows under it.
alternatives: Click a row of the table to select it; Shift-click selects the run to another row.
Click the plot to focus the nearest row.
Select a run of rows: press the button, then the last row of the run; no key is held and nothing is dragged.
drags.note: The run without a drag or a held modifier is the Select a run of rows button (Prompt 278).

drags.gesture: Drag across the image to select the pixels in the box.
alternatives: Click a pixel to focus it; the table lists every pixel as a row that a click selects.

drags.gesture: Drag on a lesson's picture (the H-R diagram, a phase plot) to set the value under the pointer.
alternatives: A click sets the value as the first press of a drag does.
The arrow keys step the value, following the picture's own axes.

drags.gesture: Drag the scene to orbit, wheel to zoom.
alternatives: The view pad under the view: four arrows that turn or move the view, and two that zoom.
The Look and Projection selects offer named views.
Arrow keys orbit, Shift pans, + and - zoom.

drags.gesture: Drag the observer's handle on the sandbox canvas to change the viewing angle.
alternatives: The Position angle slider in every observing panel (js/observerControls.js) sets the same angle: the arrow keys step it, and one press on its track moves it.
drags.note: Prompt 155 looked in index.html and js/lightCurve.js and found no control; the slider is built by js/observerControls.js, which every observing panel mounts.

drags.gesture: Drag the header of a pinned inspector card or the 3-D view window to move it; drag the 3-D window's corner to resize it.
alternatives: The Move button in the window's header: press it, then press where the top left corner goes.
With the Move button focused the arrow keys move the window (Alt a quarter of a step, Shift four).
The spacetime view's Size button does the same for the corner a drag pulls.

drags.gesture: Drag the spacetime view to orbit it, wheel to zoom, right-drag or two fingers to pan.
alternatives: The pad under the view: turn, tilt, move and zoom buttons, each one press.
drags.note: Not found by Prompt 155: the listener is the vendored OrbitControls, which the pointer-site scan does not read. Registered by Prompt 278's walk.

dragSites.about: Every module under js/ that listens for pointermove, mousemove or touchmove, and what it is. A module not listed fails tests/interactionContract.test.js until it is registered here. A drag a vendored library listens for (OrbitControls) is not seen by the scan: `vendored` names those by hand.

js/lecture.js.exempt: Shows the cursor again when the pointer moves; not a gesture.

js/main.js.exempt: The double-tap recognizer: one finger, no path.

js/observatory/imageMarks.js.exempt: A touch held on the picture shows the loupe and aims a draft; nothing is committed by it, and a tap, the nudge pad and Place do the same with no path.

js/plot/chart.js.exempt: The hover readout; the pointer only points.

js/render.js.exempt: Marks the frame loop busy for a moment; not a gesture.

inventory.about: The walk inventory (Prompt 278): one row for every surface of tools/navigation-inventory.json. e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js walks each row in English and in Spanish with real key presses: Tab from the top of the page until focus comes round (no trap, every stop named and on screen, every pressable control reached), then Tab to `reach` and `press`, which must have an effect a reader can see. `spanish: false` records a page that stays in English when Spanish is the stored choice.

exempt.manual: The printed manual is a PDF the browser's own viewer opens: it has no page of ours to walk.
